title: Yara and the Choir
premise: Marguerite Okonkwo has spent her life carving bones for the dead and keeping her gift of hearing them a secret, until she finds her own name and tonight's date in the Vellum Choir, a century-old book of prophecies. The prophecy names her as the Bone-Singer who must reforge the covenant between the living realm and the Hollow, a bargain broken when the last choir of mediums was massacred. Hunted by the moon-cult that broke the covenant and guided by the ghosts of the murdered choir, Marguerite gathers a found family of outcasts—a disgraced cartographer, a mute acolyte, and a smuggler who is more than he seems—and climbs to the Thornfell heartstone before the thirteenth moon rises. There she learns the covenant demands a life freely given; instead of dying, she offers her memory of every voice she's ever heard, becoming the new choir herself while her companions carry her story forward.
about_author: Gideon Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in West African and Alpine collections before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, craft, and the bargains we make with what we cannot bury.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. While carving a memorial bone for a drowned child, she hears the dead whisper her name alongside tonight's date—then finds both inked into the Vellum Choir, a prophecy book she's secretly kept for years. The emotional beat is dread: the invisibility she built her life around has been an illusion all along.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fleeing Thornfell village ahead of robed strangers asking about 'the bone-carver,' she takes the hidden passes only she knows and encounters Tam, a charming smuggler who claims the mountains themselves told him to find her. The beat is wary alliance—two people who trust no one deciding to travel together anyway.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned waystation, Tam watches Marguerite speak with the ghost of a murdered choir-maiden and realizes his own missing memories align with the massacre a century ago. The beat is destabilizing revelation: his charm masks a hole where his past should be.

chapters.title: The Moon-Cult's Tithe
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured briefly by the cult that broke the covenant, she learns they harvest the dead's voices to keep their leader young, and that they need her—the last true medium—to open the Hollow permanently. The beat is horror sharpening into resolve: this enemy must never win.

chapters.title: A Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The disgraced royal cartographer Isolde, exiled for mapping the Hollow's borders, rescues them and admits she's been searching for the Bone-Singer for twenty years. The beat is tentative hope: three broken people becoming, without admitting it, a company.

chapters.title: The Mute Acolyte
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In a mountain shrine they find Sefu, a cult acolyte who cut out his own voice rather than tithe it, communicating through carved bone tokens. The beat is recognition—Marguerite sees her own self-erasure mirrored in him and refuses to let him disappear.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. The company races the final ascent as the thirteenth moon waxes; the ghosts of the murdered choir manifest to guide them, but the cult ambushes at the treeline and Isolde falls protecting the maps. The beat is grief fused with fury, driving them upward through loss.

chapters.title: The Heartstone Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the heartstone, the covenant's terms reveal themselves: a life freely given. Tam offers himself, confessing he is the ghost of the choir's last survivor given flesh to find her. The beat is devastating love—she refuses his sacrifice and claims the price as her own on her terms.

chapters.title: Choir of One
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax. Rather than die, Marguerite sings every voice she's ever carried into the stone, surrendering her memories of the dead—and of her companions—as the covenant reforges and seals the Hollow against the cult. The beat is transcendent cost: victory purchased with the self.

chapters.title: The Story We Carry
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, one year later. Memory-less but alive, Marguerite carves bones in a rebuilt Thornfell while her found family surrounds her, telling her their shared stories so nothing is truly lost. The beat is bittersweet grace: found family means someone always remembers for you.
